extracted.intended_audience: Public Information Officers, Agency Administrators, family liaisons, and local unit personnel handling fatalities/serious injuries (especially in wildland fire incidents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and communication guidance for notifying next of kin, supporting families, securing scenes, collecting evidence, and coordinating investigation and staff notifications following fatalities or serious injuries during incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce defensiveness in communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Telling people what to do and starting sentences with the word “you” are common triggers for defensiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid telling people what to do and avoid starting sentences with “you.” Reduce defensiveness by avoiding general statements and instead deal with specific needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Break complicated information into small pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: The key factor to giving complicated information is breaking it into small pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume information has registered or been understood; present information in small, manageable parts to avoid misunderstanding and future problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assist family in establishing achievable goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Assist the family in establishing achievable goals (e.g., arrangements for funerals, memorials, meeting with benefits coordinator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use goal-setting to avoid problems and keep communication open. Beware of long-term family representative assignments causing over-dependence; plan a final meeting to officially end assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up contacts and referrals for benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage next of kin to begin funeral arrangements and consider return of remains, desires, travel arrangements, and agency logistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with HR to help families complete forms and processing for OWCP, SSA, VA, Public Safety Officers Benefit Program, and agency benefit claims (e.g., 401K, life insurance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain ongoing contact with family
rubrics_metrics.description: Stay in touch; initial community support often disappears after a few days or after services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide access to support programs (EAP, Wildland Firefighter Foundation), encourage networking with other affected families and coworkers, and check in frequently—this support may be needed long-term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification must be sensitive and courteous
rubrics_metrics.description: The notification process needs to be done quickly and with the utmost sensitivity; agency representative should be sensitive, courteous, sympathetic and helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your presence demonstrates agency concern; personal actions and words will reflect on the agency's image and instill confidence with survivors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of notification officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency Administrator/Line Officer or designated person is appropriate to make a notification and must be accompanied by at least one other person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider bringing a coworker, close friend, chaplain, or law enforcement officer. Always notify in person with at least two (sometimes three) people; consider separate cars in case of transportation needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare essential information before notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Key information must be gathered prior to making notification (circumstances, survivors, medical status, location of injured/deceased).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify address of next of kin, decide ahead who will speak first, obtain a private room if at workplace/hospital, and bring the Next of Kin Follow-up Worksheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine primary next of kin in order
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to Emergency Notification Information form; if not available, use standard order: spouse; parents; adult children; brothers/sisters; grandparents; legal custodians; other relatives per civil law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure correct persons are notified. Note that fiancés/significant others are not legal next of kin—ask primary next of kin if they want significant others contacted.

rubrics_metrics.name: If primary next of kin unavailable, locate or escalate
rubrics_metrics.description: If next of kin is not home, contact neighbors, police, or postmaster for information without disclosing purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If temporary absence, await return or search; if out of town and not nearby, contact nearest Agency Administrator to arrange notification actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use secondary next of kin when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: If primary next of kin is not available, contact the secondary next of kin as identified on the Emergency Notification Information sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: First visit notification protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: First visit will be difficult; be professional, demonstrate empathy and listen carefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify yourself, confirm identity of the next of kin, ask to be admitted and have them sit, never make notification on the doorstep, use victim's name, state facts clearly and succinctly (sample wording provided), and do not prolong the visit unnecessarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication: practical behaviors during notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on dress, setting, and conduct for notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be in professional attire or Class A uniform; keep visit brief and private; confirm address and phone numbers; listen and keep notes; offer to call family/friends/clergy; be inconspicuous; use the words 'died' or 'killed' (do not soften); inform that a family liaison will contact them within 24 hours; verify children correctly; leave contact names/numbers; gather follow-up worksheet info; do not promise anything you cannot deliver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited actions during notification (DON'Ts)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of actions to avoid during notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not notify primary next of kin by telephone; don't call for a prior appointment; don't hold notes or read a prepared speech; don't disclose the message to neighbors; don't use code words/acronyms; don't rush speech; don't say 'I know how you feel'; do not physically touch unless medical emergency; summon medical help for shock; limit discussion to verified information; don't rely on personal conjecture or prior experiences; don't speculate about victim activities; do not discuss funeral decisions in first visit; never make promises beyond your authority; if uncertain, say 'I do not know but will find out'; do not take personal effects on first notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and recognize family reactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals may experience shock and a range of grief reactions (shock, denial, numbness, panic, somatic distress, loneliness, depression, guilt, hostility, confusion, anger, negotiation, acceptance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange follow-up contact for the next day; allow time to react; offer to accompany to hospital/mortuary; let family decide whether to view remains; grief recovery is long-term and requires continued contact and support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling inquiries about injured persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Next of kin will ask where their loved one is and how to arrange to see them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify location and status before arrival; if seriously injured, immediately arrange transportation to the medical facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain status and timing of remains
rubrics_metrics.description: Remains may not be immediately recoverable; normally not available until 24–36 hours after autopsy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain causes for delay (autopsy, medical reasons, criminal investigation, travel documentation) and proactively follow up on status; do not wait for next of kin to ask.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal effects handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal effects should be gathered from incident site/home immediately but not delivered at first notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver effects later in a clean unmarked box; clean or make presentable clothing; anticipate delays due to investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up contact content
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency Administrator/notifier should follow up as agreed to check next of kin welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express concern, offer assistance, answer unresolved questions (site visits, travel arrangements, timing of remains), allow next of kin time to talk, and follow through on promises and obligations; staying in touch may last years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify coworkers appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Notify coworkers who had close relationships with the deceased/injured in person—not by voicemail or email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify employees at current and prior workstations as applicable; never delay family notification for coworker notification; consider temporary relief from duty; ensure access to CISM/EAP or counseling; monitor wellbeing and provide follow-up; allow employees to attend funerals/memorials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification for public victims or contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: When the victim is a member of the public or a contractor employee, different notification channels apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the victim is a member of the public, law enforcement should notify. If the victim is a contractor employee, notify the contractor's home office per contract specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Next of Kin Follow-Up Worksheet during notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the Next of Kin Follow-Up Worksheet at the time of notification to record surviving family members and their wishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect next of kin name, contact info, relation, funeral home preference, viewing preference, special items, others to contact, support persons, date/time, and notifier signature; retain worksheet for continuity of follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely reporting of wildland fire fatalities/entrapments to NICC
rubrics_metrics.description: For wildland fire fatalities, entrapments and burnovers, notify the National Interagency Coordination Center (208-387-5400) within 24 hours and use NWCG Form PMS 405-1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit written report to NICC within 24 hours even if some data are missing; immediate phone notification to NICC Coordinator on Duty is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure the incident scene for investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of rescue/medical assistance, the scene must be secured until released by the accident investigation team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods include ropes, barrier tape, cones, signs, flashing lights, and posted guards. Do not move equipment, shelters, or other items; do not walk around unless necessary for rescue; preserve evidence; photograph/video scene if evidence might be lost before investigators arrive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request autopsy for all fatalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Request an autopsy for all fatalities and offer to pay if funding is an issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a liaison to the county medical examiner/coroner; obtain access to 911 logs and police reports if needed. For fire-related fatalities, provide the FA 156 Firefighter Autopsy Protocol to the medical examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness statement procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify witnesses and have them write, date and sign statements before leaving if they must be released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate witnesses, have them write statements in their own words and handwriting (or typed by them). Statements should include name/address/phone, time/location, what attracted attention, sequence of events, environment (weather, lighting, noise), positions of people/equipment, what was moved, actions the witness took, and other involved people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement Critical Incident Stress Management (CISM) as needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine need for and level of CISM and implement accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise the Serious Accident Investigation Team (SAIT) of CISM actions taken. Provide peer support or professional resources as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide administrative support to Accident Investigation Team
rubrics_metrics.description: The investigation team will need a local unit liaison and logistical/administrative support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate a liaison not directly involved in the accident; provide lodging/meeting place/private interview rooms; office supplies (flip charts, markers); documentation support (shredder, fax, computers, printer, vehicles, speaker phones, copier) as coordinated with the team leader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive evidence collection checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect applicable documents and items for investigation (job hazard analyses, radio/dispatch logs, maps, briefings, training and medical records, qualifications, timesheets, equipment records, inspection documents, plans, press releases, autopsy/toxicology reports, death certificate, 911 log, witness statements, tailgate safety documentation, unit safety plan, incident action plans, personnel lists, internal policies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not collect evidence at the scene unless in danger of disappearing; contact the investigation team leader or chief investigator before removing evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designate key contacts (family liaison, PAO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Designate someone to serve as family liaison and Public Affairs Officer for media interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Family liaison maintains open communication with the family and provides support, assistance, and information. Contact the agency PAO if significant media interest arises.
